messages:
anya: quick heads-up — seeing a latency tail on the 8xA100 cluster when running TP+PP with KV sharding. p95 jumped ~30% after the kernel update yesterday. nvprof shows big NCCL peaks during decode. anyone else?
joel: saw it too. root cause looks like all-reduce spikes around step 1..3 of decode. KV hits are lower than expected (cache miss rate ~12%). sharing nsys snippet below: 

```
nsys profile summary:
  total kernels: 1432
  cudaMemcpy/Async: 6.2%
  ncclAllReduce: 22.1% 
  attention kernels (fused): 38.5%
  idle/wait (sync): 9.8%
```

joel: NVTX timing shows NCCL calls blocking on stream 0 instead of async stream, so comm/compute overlap poor.
sam: what sharding strategy are you using for KV? pure shard across TP dims or hybrid?
anya: pure TP shard right now — each TP rank holds a kv slice. PP is layering on top (2-stage), DP replicas = 2.
phil: pure TP shard -> requires all-gather/all-reduce during causal decode to build full KV for each query, that's the comm spike. In PP, if the KV lives on upstream stage, you also move tensors between stages which adds latency. DP avoids cross-rank comm but doubles KV memory. tradeoffs.
maria: from memory/latency POV we should consider hybrid: replicate recent short prefixes across DP within same host (cheap) and shard long prefixes across TP. that reduces all-reduce frequency for short queries which are the majority.
eva: +1. Also try switching NCCL to asynchronous progress and move NCCL ops onto dedicated comm streams. quick patch: set NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 and create a cudaStream for nccl that runs concurrently. saw 10-15% tail reduction before.
anya: posting config I tested locally — small change to runtime config for sharding/prefetch: 

```yaml
kv_shard_policy: hybrid
  replicate_prefix_tokens: 64  # replicate first 64 tokens across TP ranks
  shard_threshold: 512        # if seq_len > 512, shard remainder across TP
comm:
  use_async_nccl_stream: true
  nccl_stream_priority: low
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 16384
  prefer_length_buckets: true
  bucket_sizes: [32, 128, 512]
kernel_flags:
  enable_flash_attn: true
  fused_qkv: true
  cublas_workspace_mb: 256
```

phil: nice. also consider reordering decode to prefetch KV shards for the next token while current token is computing attention — pipeline the prefetch on a separate stream. that helps hide comm.
joel: profiler after hybrid patch (local microbench): 
```
nsys summary after:
  ncclAllReduce: 9.7%
  attention kernels: 41.2%
  memcpy/async: 4.8%
  idle/wait: 6.1%
p95 latency: -18%
cache_miss_rate: 4.5%
```
joel: promising but this was single-host test; multi-host will still see inter-node NVLINK/NIC cost.
anya: any thoughts on kernel selection? the recent fused-attn patch might have unintended memlayout that increases memcpy before NCCL.
sam: check cublasLt vs cublasGemmEx ordering. sometimes fused kernels reorder q/k/v layout to packed form which triggers an extra transpose. if we can keep qkv layout native to fused kernel we avoid extra device copies.
maria: we should add microbench harness that runs: 1) TP-only KV-shard, 2) PP-only (KV on last stage), 3) hybrid, 4) DP-replicated baseline. collect p50/p95, nccl time, memcpy, and peak gpu mem. tag with model size and seq len.
eva: infra-bot kicked off nightly perf job for that set. infra-bot: scheduled perf_matrix/kv_shard_experiment on cluster x-8a100, ETA 6h. logs to /perf/kv_shard/1769904321.
anya: next steps: (1) run the microbench above across multi-host, (2) try async NCCL + comm stream patch, (3) enable hybrid policy in canary, (4) validate quality/regression. I'll open a PR for the hybrid sharding flags and the async-nccl stream plumbing.
phil: add a small telemetry event for cache_miss_rate + allreduce_time_per_token so we can correlate on canary.
joel: also add a stress test with long convo prefix > 2048 tokens to ensure we don't regress tail.
anya: thanks all — filing follow-ups in the perf board. ping me if you want access to the infra run results. :thumbsup:
